hook: Scientists just modeled the first 2 billion years of our universe.

sections.voiceover: Scientists just modeled the first 2 billion years of our universe.
sections.visual_cue: A vast, swirling cosmic web of dark matter glowing in deep space.
sections.sfx_cue: Low, resonant bass hum building in intensity.
b_roll: NASA artist rendition of early universe filaments

sections.voiceover: Researchers at MIT and Harvard University created the Lumina simulation to map this ancient era. How did they capture such detail?
sections.visual_cue: Split screen showing logos of MIT and Harvard, transitioning to a wide map of space.

sections.voiceover: Lumina tracks 432 billion particles to recreate the evolution of the early universe across time.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of a dense cluster of particles assembling into a web structure.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of rapid particle collision clicks.
b_roll: Scientific animation of particle density mapping

sections.voiceover: Lumina finally brings the first 2 billion years of our universe into sharp, clear focus.
sections.visual_cue: Zooming into a small, bright pocket of the cosmic web.

sections.voiceover: We are witnessing the infancy of the universe within this 1.6 billion light-year simulation region.
sections.visual_cue: Slow pull-back to show the entire simulated universe structure.
b_roll: Wide shot of simulated cosmic web filaments
